body.description: Architecture principle for the Haskell line (Krzysztof, 2026-07-24): depart from the Data.* mixbag into DDD domains and bounded contexts, read as Kripke semantics meets sheaves. Naming: the DOMAIN IS THE ROOT namespace — no vendor prefix, no technical category (cf. Mosaic.Voronoi, Noise.Simplex, Discourse.Domain, Logic.Judgement); the second segment is a genuine notion within that world. For the fork: Board.*, Execution.*, Memory.*, possibly Discourse.* (comment/thread fabric). Concretely: (1) each bounded context is a world with its own local ontology — no shared God-types; (2) context overlaps are explicit restriction maps (anti-corruption translations) onto shared interface modules; (3) the sheaf condition is the consistency law — local views agreeing on overlaps glue into global sections; global truth is glued, never primitive; (4) accessibility (which world may refer into which) is explicit in the import/morphism structure; (5) the event firehose is the natural gluing site. Ubiquities (Ubiquity.*) = the constant sheaf: tiny frozen substrate in every world (ids, timestamps, workspace scoping, actor refs). Supporting/generic subdomains (auth, delivery, storage plumbing) serve core worlds without owning meaning. Guard: misfiling as ubiquitous is how God-types sneak back — default world-local until gluing forces promotion. First deliverable on the Haskell mark: derive the context/overlap diagram from Protocol's comprehension maps before cutting any package.
body.title: Bounded contexts as Kripke worlds, glued sheaf-wise
